features.name: Why the open questions matter
features.label: The most useful thing on this screen. Send these before you build, not after.
features.promise: The card tells you its questions are the most valuable thing on the screen and should be sent before building.
features.howToVerify: Load the brief and confirm the sentence renders under the card heading.

features.name: A blocking open question
features.label: Blocking — What should happen when metrics-server is missing?
features.promise: A question card marked Blocking with an alert icon states the question and why it cannot be guessed.
features.howToVerify: Load the brief and confirm the Blocking badge, the question and the rationale all render, and that the card is visually distinct from the non-blocking ones.
features.notes: Different fill/stroke (fill_ZSJSX1 / stroke_5WTRNW) from the 'Worth asking' cards. Severity is a real distinction, not decoration.

features.name: A 'Worth asking' question about the window
features.label: Worth asking — Is 24 hours the right window?
features.promise: A question card marked 'Worth asking' with a search icon, the question and supporting evidence.
features.howToVerify: Load the brief and confirm the badge, question and evidence line render.

features.name: A 'Worth asking' question about the Conditions column
features.label: Worth asking — Replace the Conditions column, or sit beside it?
features.promise: A second 'Worth asking' card with its question and the risk of getting it wrong.
features.howToVerify: Load the brief and confirm the badge, question and rationale render.

features.name: Ask the requester
features.label: Ask the requester
features.promise: Every question card has a button that sends that one question to whoever raised the ticket.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Ask the requester' on the blocking question and confirm that question is sent and the masthead count drops from 3 to 2.
features.notes: One per question: 34:1100, 34:1116, 34:1132. Should interact with 34:980's count.

features.name: Answer it myself
features.label: Answer it myself
features.promise: Every question card has a button that lets you answer the question yourself instead of sending it.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Answer it myself' on a question and confirm an input appears, that the answer can be typed and saved, and that the question stops counting as open.
features.notes: One per question: 34:1105, 34:1121, 34:1137. The input it opens is not drawn on this screen, so its form is inferred, but that it takes typed input is not.

features.name: Prior art was checked
features.label: Checked against every extension and Rancher page on this instance.
features.promise: The card claims the assistant checked the whole instance for overlapping functionality.
features.howToVerify: Load the brief and confirm the sentence renders; the claim is only honest if the list below comes from the real instance rather than fixtures.
features.notes: A claim about real work. Worth checking whether the entries are actually derived from the running Rancher.

features.name: Existing cluster dashboard entry
features.label: Cluster dashboard
features.promise: An entry names an existing Rancher page that already covers part of the request, and says what it does and does not cover.
features.howToVerify: Load the brief and confirm the entry renders with its name and description.

features.name: Look at it
features.label: Look at it
features.promise: A ghost button opens the existing cluster dashboard so you can judge the overlap yourself.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Look at it' and confirm the cluster dashboard opens.

features.name: Existing longhorn-capacity extension entry
features.label: longhorn-capacity extension
features.promise: An entry names an installed extension that already draws the same 24-hour bar pattern, with a note on consistency.
features.howToVerify: Load the brief and confirm the entry renders with its name and description.

features.name: Reuse its chart
features.label: Reuse its chart
features.promise: A ghost button adopts the existing extension's chart for this brief rather than drawing a new one.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Reuse its chart' and confirm the choice is recorded on the brief (and reaches the agent when building starts).
features.notes: A real commitment, not navigation: it should change what gets built.

features.name: Scroll the brief
features.promise: The two-column body scrolls independently of the masthead, so the brief can be longer than the viewport while the action buttons stay put.
features.howToVerify: Load the brief in a short viewport and confirm the columns scroll while the masthead with 'Agree and start building' stays visible.
features.notes: Frame is literally named 'scroll' and wraps the columns; the masthead sits outside it.
